instruction: Grade Richard Smith's exam (answer_sheet1.docx) against the reference answers. Fill in 1 for correct, 0 for incorrect in his row of the grades spreadsheet, and enter the total grade.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to grade 9 students' English exams by writing a Python script. It installed python-docx and openpyxl, extracted the answer key (Q1:D,Q2:A,...,Q10:D), and began writing code to parse student answer sheets. However, it spent all 47 turns in the terminal writing/debugging Python code and never entered any data into the spreadsheet.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate between LibreOffice windows (Calc, Writer), open files from file manager, use terminal to install packages and write Python scripts, understand spreadsheet structure and the grading task concept
metadata.failure_analysis: Model tried to automate the entire grading process via Python script instead of manually entering data or completing the script. It ran out of turns (47) without ever updating the spreadsheet. The original task required grading 9 students which was too complex.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to grading just one student (Richard Smith) to reduce complexity while keeping the same cross-application workflow
metadata.explanation: Evaluator reads row 3 (Richard Smith) cells C3:M3 from grades.xlsx and checks Q1-Q10 scores and Total Grade against expected values. Partial credit: each correct cell worth 1/11 of total score.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads row 3, columns C(3) to M(13) from grades.xlsx, extracting 11 values (Q1-Q10 scores + total grade) for Richard Smith's row
Metric correctly accesses expected.get('expected_values') — proper handling of rule-type expected parameter (receives rules dict directly)
Partial credit logic is sound: each of the 11 cells contributes 1/11 to final score, with float/int comparison and None handling
Postconfig properly activates grades.xlsx window and saves with Ctrl+S before getter reads file, ensuring fresh state
Expected values [1,1,0,1,1,0,1,0,1,1,70] are internally consistent: 7 correct out of 10 questions = 70 total grade
Both instruction requirements are covered: individual question scores (1/0) AND total grade entry
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Cannot independently verify expected answer correctness (which specific questions Richard Smith got right/wrong) without access to the actual exam documents (answer_sheet1.docx and ReferenceAnswers.docx). The values rely on the task author's grading being accurate.
Consider adding a sheet name parameter explicitly rather than defaulting to worksheets[0], in case the spreadsheet has multiple sheets
